result.summary: This pull request replaces out-of-band interrupt methods (`interrupt()` and `interruptWait()`) on blocking `interfaces::Mining` methods (`waitTipChanged`, `createNewBlock`, and `BlockTemplate::waitNext`) with native Cap'n Proto request cancellation arguments (`CancelArg`). It adds C++ and Cap'n Proto glue to register cancellation callbacks with request contexts and clean them up with a guard object. It also updates functional and unit tests to exercise promise cancellation.
result.problem: Blocking mining calls currently require separate, out-of-band IPC calls to interrupt them when in progress, adding protocol complexity and potential race conditions for multi-process mining clients.

resolved_concerns: Moved CancelArg and serialization helpers out of libmultiprocess into interfaces/types.h and ipc/capnp/common-types.h following upstream changes.
Added CancelGuard to unregister the cancellation callback when the wrapped method finishes, preventing execution after scope exit.

result.card: This PR replaces out-of-band interrupt methods for blocking mining calls (such as waitNext and createNewBlock) with native Cap'n Proto request cancellation arguments. By introducing CancelArg to interfaces::Mining, external clients like Stratum v2 template providers can abort pending calls directly using native RPC cancellation rather than issuing separate interrupt requests. ryanofsky strongly supported the approach as a cleaner, more efficient mechanism for external multi-language clients. The branch depends on unmerged upstream changes in libmultiprocess (bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess#342) and CI is currently failing.
